Durability – Openings in the soffits, gables, mushroom and ridge vents allow more than just air to enter the attic. In cold northern climates snow can be blown in through these openings, accumulating, melting and causing damage to the ceiling or creating the potential premature structural failure or mold growth inside the roof assembly. In coastal climates wind driven rain can be blown in through these openings with similar results. In areas subject to wildfires, burning embers can be blown in through these openings, potentially starting roof fires.
Why Use Closed-Cell Spray Polyurethane Foam (ccSPF)?
Closed-cell spray polyurethane foam can be used to create an unvented roof assembly that works in all climate zones. The design approach is the same for all climate zones.
There are currently two types of spray polyurethane foam (SPF) insulation used in North American residential construction:  ccSPF or closed-cell medium-density spray foam (”2 pound” or 2 pounds per cubic foot) and ocSPF or open-cell low-density spray foam (“half pound” or 0.5 pcf). When installed properly, both adhere to most construction surfaces and expand to fill voids and create an air seal. Closed-cell spray foam made with EPA-approved HFC blowing agents like, Honeywell Enovate 245fa, has a higher thermal resistance (e.g. is a better insulation) and lower vapor permeance than open-cell spray foam. Closed-cell spray foam acts as an air barrier (at 1 in. or 25 mm minimum thickness) and vapor retarder (at 2 in. or 50 mm minimum thickness*) and therefore does not need an additional vapor retarder in cold climates).
Unvented roof assemblies with ccSPF work well in all climate zones and serve several important functions:
Controls Airflow – ccSPF is air impermeable, adheres well to almost all construction surfaces and expands to fill voids creating an air seal and eliminating air leakage. In cold climates it prevents warm, humid indoor air from reaching the back (underside) of roof sheathing where it can condense. In warm climates it prevents humid outside air that enters the roof due to natural and/or controlled ventilation from reaching the back of the roof sheathing, which can be cooled below the air temperature by night sky radiation (i.e. the effect that causes dew).
Control Heat Flow – Closed-cell spray foam has exceptional thermal performance relative to other insulations (i.e. the highest R-value per inch.) ccSPF can be used to create a very compact roof assembly that meets or exceeds the code required thermal performance.
Control Vapor Diffusion – Closed-cell spray foam acts as a throttle to control the rate of vapor diffusion. The foam insulation resists the diffusion of water vapor so that the amount of water vapor is reduced as it moves through the thickness of the foam. By the time the water vapor reaches the back of the roof sheathing, there is not enough left to cause condensation problems.
In cold climates the ccSPF provides the first condensing plane. The ccSPF should be installed directly to the face (i.e. back) of the roof sheathing in a layer thick enough to prevent condensation from forming on the inside face of the foam.
In hot climates up to 5 in.* (125 mm) of ccSPF can also be used. In this application the assembly can still dry to the inside during the daytime when roof temperatures are high (120-190°F or 50-90°C), the vapor pressure gradients are very large (5-35 kPa) and the foam is a vapor retarder and not a vapor barrier.
Controls Rain Leakage – Closed-cell spray foam has negligible water permeability, minimal water absorption, and excellent adhesion allowing it to act as a secondary rainwater barrier to limit damage when primary roof assembly rainwater control membranes leak. Rainwater migration is severely limited due to the low water transmission and high adhesion (“waterproofing”) characteristics of the foam and damage is limited to the area immediately adjacent the hole in the primary rainwater control membrane. This tends to contain the damage, making it easier to identify the source and preventing it from spreading throughout the assembly and to interior finishes which can be costly to repair.

Practical Recommendation for a 10x12 Climate-Controlled Shed For a standard 10x12 outbuilding (120 sq. ft. floor, ~320 net sq. ft. walls, ~150 sq. ft. roof/ceiling), the ideal year-round climate-controlled assembly that balances thermal resistance, airtightness, acoustic isolation, and DIY buildability is **Strategy 2 (Mineral Wool + Rigid Foam Hybrid)**. ### A. Recommended Wall Assembly - **Framing:** Standard 2x4 framing at 16" on-center. - **Exterior Weather Barrier:** Exterior sheathing (OSB or plywood) wrapped with a water-resistive barrier (DuPont Tyvek HomeWrap) with taped seams, behind standard siding on rainscreen furring strips (or direct-applied siding). - **Cavity Insulation:** **ROCKWOOL Comfortbatt R-15** (3.5" thickness, 15" width). Friction-fit firmly between studs with no gaps or compression. - **Interior Finish:** 1/2" drywall (taped and primed with vapor-retardant latex paint) or 1/2" interior plywood. An interior 6-mil poly sheet should be **omitted** to prevent a double vapor barrier that traps summer humidity. ### B. Recommended Roof / Ceiling Assembly - **Framing:** 2x6 roof rafters at 16" or 24" on-center. - **Ventilation:** Continuous vented soffit at the eaves connected to upper gable louvers or a continuous ridge vent. Install **Amerimax Accuvent** baffles (or Durovent) in every rafter bay against the roof deck to guarantee a 1" to 1.5" continuous air channel. - **Cavity Insulation:** **ROCKWOOL Comfortbatt R-15** installed below the baffles within the rafter bays. - **Continuous Thermal Break & Air Barrier:** **2" Owens Corning FOAMULAR NGX F-250 XPS (R-10)** panels fastened directly across the underside of the rafters using 3" construction screws through 1.25" Go Board / plastic insulation washers. - **Air Sealing:** Seal all board perimeter perimeters and penetrations with low-expansion Great Stuff Pro Window & Door polyurethane foam, and tape all board butt-joints with DuPont Tyvek Acrylic Construction Tape. This creates an airtight, continuous interior ceiling plane providing **R-25 total resistance** and completely stopping warm, humid indoor air from reaching the cold roof deck. ### C. Recommended Floor Assembly - **Sub-Base:** Ground cleared and sloped away from the shed, covered with a heavy **6-mil polyethylene sheet** ballasted with gravel to stop rising ground moisture. Pier blocks or skids elevate the shed floor framing at least 6" off the ground for cross-ventilation. - **Framing:** Pressure-treated 2x6 floor joists at 16" on-center. - **Insulation:** **2" Owens Corning FOAMULAR NGX XPS (R-10)** rigid foam boards cut to width and friction-fitted between the joists, supported by 1x2 ledger strips or corrosion-resistant screws. Seal all perimeter gaps between foam and joists with canned expanding foam to block air infiltration and rodent intrusion. - **Subfloor:** 3/4" tongue-and-groove exterior-grade OSB or plywood glued to the joists with subfloor construction adhesive (e.g., Liquid Nails) and screwed down. - **Finished Floor:** Luxury vinyl plank (LVP) with integrated waterproof underlayment. ### D. Climate Control Pairing Pair this tight envelope with an appropriately sized **9,000 BTU mini-split heat pump** (or a dual-hose inverter window heat pump). In a 120 sq. ft. space with an R-15/R-25/R-10 envelope, a mini-split will operate at minimum modulation, maintain exact workspace temperatures in sub-freezing winters or hot summers, and actively dehumidify the air to eliminate indoor moisture accumulation. --- ## 4.
